'''Bikya''' (also known as '''Furu''') is a potentially extinct [[Southern Bantoid languages|Southern Bantoid]] language spoken in [[Cameroon]]. It is one of the three, or four, [[Furu languages]]. In 1986 four surviving speakers were identified, although only one (a man in his seventies) spoke the language fluently.

English linguist Dr. David Dalby filmed{{When|date=December 2024}} an 87-year-old [[Native ethnic groups of Africa|African]] woman who spoke Bikya as her native tongue. At the time, it was believed that she was the last Bikya speaker.<ref name="oneleft">{{cite news |last1=Dyer |first1=Gwynne |title=Profusion of tongues in the global village |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/bs-xpm-1997-10-02-1997275054-story.html |access-date=22 December 2020 |work=[[Baltimore Sun]]}}</ref>

It, and presumably all of Furu, is perhaps a [[Beboid language]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Blench|first=Roger|title=The membership and internal structure of Bantoid and the border with Bantu|date=7–9 April 2011|url=https://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/Bantoid/General/Blench%20Bantu%20IV%20Berlin%20Bantoid%202011.pdf|access-date=5 March 2024}}</ref>
